title: "Report 6 · Vote intention"
---

```{r}
#| include: false
source("../R/report_setup.R")
category_order <- c("CDU/CSU", "SPD", "FDP", "Greens", "Die Linke", "AfD", "Other party",
                    "Would not vote", "Don't know yet", "No answer", "UNRECOGNISED")
d$vote <- factor(d$vote, levels = category_order)
```

## What is measured

The "Sunday question": *Which party would you vote for if the election for the German Bundestag were next Sunday?* This is **stated intention**, not observed voting. The answers are stored as German text labels and translated in `R/prepare_data.R`. All `r length(unique(d$exercise_id))` respondents took part in all five waves; results are unweighted and are **not** estimates of German election results.

**The answer options changed.** "I would not vote" and "I don't know yet" were offered only from wave 2. In wave 1, people in these situations had to skip the question or choose a party. This explains the larger number of missing answers in wave 1, and it means wave 1 is not directly comparable with later waves. Switching analyses therefore use waves 2-5.

## Categories and frequencies by wave

Cells with fewer than `r MIN_CELL` respondents are shown as "<`r MIN_CELL`".

```{r}
counts <- table(d$vote, d$wave)
shares <- prop.table(counts, 2)
freq   <- matrix(sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", counts, 100 * shares), nrow = nrow(counts))
freq[counts < MIN_CELL] <- paste0("<", MIN_CELL)
freq[rownames(counts) %in% c("Would not vote", "Don't know yet") & counts[, 1] == 0, 1] <- "not offered"
freq <- data.frame(Category = rownames(counts), freq)
names(freq)[-1] <- paste0("W", colnames(counts))
show_table(freq[rowSums(counts) > 0, ])
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 7
valid  <- d[!is.na(d$vote_group), ]
shares <- as.data.frame(prop.table(table(Wave = valid$wave, Group = valid$vote_group), 1))
shares$Wave <- paste0("W", shares$Wave)
ggplot(shares, aes(Wave, Freq, colour = Group, group = Group)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(round(100 * x), "%")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of valid answers", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

**Not identifiable in this extract:** "Other party" grows in later waves. This may reflect new parties (for example BSW, founded in 2024), but the extract has no open-text answers, so this cannot be checked.

## Switching between waves

For switching, parties are grouped to avoid very small cells: FDP, Die Linke and "other party" form **Other parties**; "would not vote" and "don't know yet" form **Undecided / non-voter**. Respondents without an answer in one of the two waves are left out of that comparison.

```{r}
# vote group of the same respondents in two waves
vote_pair <- function(w1, w2) {
  a <- d[d$wave == w1, c("exercise_id", "vote_group")]
  b <- d[d$wave == w2, c("exercise_id", "vote_group")]
  m <- merge(a, b, by = "exercise_id")
  names(m) <- c("id", "from", "to")
  m[!is.na(m$from) & !is.na(m$to), ]
}

switch_pattern <- function(from, to) {
  undecided <- "Undecided / non-voter"
  ifelse(from == undecided & to == undecided, "Stayed undecided / non-voter",
  ifelse(from == undecided,                   "Undecided / non-voter to a party",
  ifelse(to == undecided,                     "Party to undecided / non-voter",
  ifelse(from == to,                          "Same party",
                                              "Switched to another party"))))
}

transition_table <- function(w1, w2) {
  p   <- vote_pair(w1, w2)
  tab <- table(p$from, p$to)
  out <- matrix(ifelse(tab < MIN_CELL, paste0("<", MIN_CELL), tab), nrow = nrow(tab))
  out <- data.frame(rownames(tab), out)
  names(out) <- c("From (rows) / to (columns)", colnames(tab))
  out
}
```

**Summary of switching patterns** (same respondents, adjacent waves):

```{r}
patterns <- c("Same party", "Switched to another party", "Party to undecided / non-voter",
              "Undecided / non-voter to a party", "Stayed undecided / non-voter")
summary_table <- data.frame(Pattern = patterns)
for (w in 2:4) {
  p <- vote_pair(w, w + 1)
  n <- as.vector(table(factor(switch_pattern(as.character(p$from), as.character(p$to)), levels = patterns)))
  summary_table[[paste0("W", w, " to W", w + 1)]] <-
    ifelse(n < MIN_CELL, paste0("<", MIN_CELL), sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(p)))
}
show_table(summary_table)
```

**Wave 2 to wave 3:**

```{r}
show_table(transition_table(2, 3))
```

**Wave 3 to wave 4:**

```{r}
show_table(transition_table(3, 4))
```

**Wave 4 to wave 5:**

```{r}
show_table(transition_table(4, 5))
```

## Vote intention and the assigned constructs

**Design.** A later measure should never explain an earlier answer, so the construct scores come from an **earlier wave** than the vote: scores in wave 4 predict vote intention in wave 5. The same model is repeated with wave 3 scores and wave 4 vote as a replication. Support for rehabilitation exists only from wave 3, so wave 3 is the earliest possible start.

**Model.** Multinomial logistic regression: the six grouped vote categories are the outcome, and all six construct scores (standardised) are the predictors. To make the result readable, the figure shows how the **average predicted probability** of each category changes when one score moves from 1 SD below to 1 SD above the mean, with the other scores kept at their observed values. The 95% intervals come from 300 bootstrap samples. These are associations in a non-random panel, not causal effects.

```{r}
predictors <- c("rwa", "anomie", "rel_deprivation", "rehabilitation", "attr_societal", "attr_individual")

# scores in wave w_in, vote group in wave w_out, same respondents
model_data <- function(w_in, w_out) {
  x <- d[d$wave == w_in,  c("exercise_id", predictors)]
  y <- d[d$wave == w_out, c("exercise_id", "vote_group")]
  m <- merge(x, y, by = "exercise_id")
  m <- m[complete.cases(m), ]
  m[predictors] <- scale(m[predictors])
  m$vote_group <- droplevels(m$vote_group)
  m
}

# change in predicted probability, -1 SD to +1 SD, for every predictor
probability_change <- function(m) {
  fit <- nnet::multinom(vote_group ~ ., data = m[c("vote_group", predictors)], trace = FALSE)
  out <- NULL
  for (p in predictors) {
    low  <- m; low[[p]]  <- -1
    high <- m; high[[p]] <-  1
    change <- colMeans(predict(fit, high, type = "probs")) - colMeans(predict(fit, low, type = "probs"))
    out <- rbind(out, data.frame(Predictor = score_names[[p]], Category = names(change), Change = change))
  }
  out
}

with_bootstrap <- function(m, reps = 300) {
  set.seed(2026)
  result <- probability_change(m)
  boot <- replicate(reps, {
    b <- tryCatch(probability_change(m[sample(nrow(m), replace = TRUE), ])$Change,
                  error = function(e) NULL)
    if (length(b) == nrow(result)) b else rep(NA, nrow(result))
  })
  result$lo <- apply(boot, 1, quantile, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)
  result$hi <- apply(boot, 1, quantile, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)
  result
}

effect_plot <- function(result) {
  ggplot(result, aes(100 * Change, Predictor)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = 100 * lo, xmax = 100 * hi), size = .3) +
    facet_wrap(~ Category, nrow = 2) +
    labs(x = "Change in predicted probability, -1 SD to +1 SD (percentage points)", y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10)
}

m45 <- model_data(4, 5)
m34 <- model_data(3, 4)
r45 <- with_bootstrap(m45)
r34 <- with_bootstrap(m34)
```

### Main model: scores in wave 4, vote intention in wave 5

Analytic n = `r nrow(m45)`. Respondents per category: `r paste(names(table(m45$vote_group)), table(m45$vote_group), collapse = "; ")`.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-width: 9
effect_plot(r45)
```

```{r}
show_table(data.frame(Predictor = r45$Predictor, Category = r45$Category,
                      `Change (percentage points)` = 100 * r45$Change,
                      `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.1f, %.1f]", 100 * r45$lo, 100 * r45$hi),
                      check.names = FALSE), digits = 1)
```

### Replication: scores in wave 3, vote intention in wave 4

Analytic n = `r nrow(m34)`.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-width: 9
effect_plot(r34)
```

## Interpretation and limits

*TODO (Monika): 3-5 sentences, written after reading the results above. Which constructs go with which party choice, does the replication agree, and what can and cannot be concluded?*

- Stated intention, not behaviour; an unweighted panel of people who stayed for five waves.
- Wave 1 had different answer options and is used only descriptively.
- The party groups combine parties with different profiles (for example FDP and Die Linke) to keep cells large enough; this hides differences inside a group.
- The scores are measured one wave before the vote, but this does not make the association causal: stable traits and earlier vote intention may explain both.
